newsitem.title: USA: Kmart to merge Canada functions; 150 job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Kmart to merge Canada functions; 150 job cuts.

text.p: Kmart Corp. said on Wednesday it will cut 150 jobs in Canada and merge some functions with its U.S. business to save $10 million to $20 million a year, and it still may sell its Canadian unit in the future.
Kmart, the nation's second-largest retailer, said the realignment was part of an effort to take the 125-store Canadian chain out of the red, perhaps by next year.
The changes came almost a year after Troy, Mich.-based Kmart ended talks about selling the division to Hudson's Bay Co. and decided instead to revitalize it.

"What we're doing is working very, very hard to restore this company to appropriate levels of profitability," said Martin Welch, Kmart's chief financial officer. "The better it gets, the less inclined we're going to be to get rid of it."
The retailer has not held recent conversations with any suitors. Kmart Canada employs about 12,000 workers.

The Canadian operation's same-store sales, or sales among store open at least a year, were flat during September, and it will not be profitable this year, although the retailer hopes to rebound next year, said Michael Lynch, chief executive of Kmart Canada.
"That certainly is our goal," he said.

It has closed four stores this year and could shut a few more after a review scheduled to take place in the first quarter of next year, he said. On Wednesday, the company sent vendors in Canada a letter stating its parent will provide the division with working capital to make it through the crucial holiday season.
Meanwhile, Kmart is working to sell seven shopping centers and a distribution center in Canada and lease them back from potential buyers.

After the realignment, about 200 positions will remain in the Kmart Canada's head office in Brampton, Ontario, and a number of new positions will be created in Troy, Mich., where Kmart is based, the company said. It was not specific about the number of new U.S. jobs.

Kmart Canada's financial, systems, store operations and other administrative support functions will be merged into Kmart's headquarters in Troy, beginning in October. The merger will be completed in 1997.
The parent company is looking to sell other assets.

Its troubled Builders Square building supply chain remains on the auction block. Kmart has talked to suitors, but since it has guaranteed Builders Squares' leases, it wants to be sure the buyer is capable of running the business well.

"If we don't think the potential acquiror has a high probability of running the business successfully, it does not make sense for us to sell the business only to get it back in 18 or 24 months in worse shape," Welch said.
Kmart's sales in the United States also have been poor.

Analysts estimate that its same-store sales, or sales among stores open at least a year in the United States, were flat in September. Kmart and other large U.S. retailers will report sales results on Thursday.

Sales should pick up before Christmas, the retailer said. It expects same-store sales to rise by about 3 percent during the holidays. That compares to a gain of about 5 percent that Merrill Lynch is forecasting for the industry for November and December of this year.
Kmart's stock ended down 25 cents to $10.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
